tone noun

of voice

also tone of voice, in that tone, an angry tone, a gentle tone

classical

Gell. 1.26.8: ex vōce
Cic. de Or. 3.216 (Lewis & Short: “a voice, sound, tone”)

vōx, vōcis f.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

the voice; its tone

Latin speaks of the voice itself, which takes on the colour of each feeling (Cic. de Or. 3.216–219); it also means a word, a saying, a language, and an accent (rūstica vōx et agrestis, de Or. 3.42).

Other words

  • sonus, sonī m. — the sound of a voice; tone, character

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Gell. 13.20.12: sonus vōcis (Lewis & Short, s.v. injūcundus); Cic. Opt. Gen. 1: suus est cuique certus sonus (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    A sound or noise, and in Cicero the tone or style of a speech or a genre.

  • vōcis genus — a kind of voice, a tone

    also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 3.217: vōcis genus crēbrō incīdēns (Lewis & Short, s.v. incīdō)

    Cicero’s phrase for the tone a speaker takes for each feeling: here a voice broken by sobs.

Examples

  • nunc ego tibi īrāscī videor? ex vultūne meō an ex vōce an ex colōre an etiam ex verbīs correptum esse mē īrā intellegis?

    do I seem angry to you now? Is it from my face, or my tone, or my colour, or my words that you gather I am in the grip of anger?Gell. 1.26.8

  • et in cēterīs suus est cuique certus sonus

    and in the other kinds each has its own fixed toneCic. Opt. Gen. 1 (Lewis & Short)

See also loud, in a low voice, lower your voice, volume.
